A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LatentMAS. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, figures, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark accuracy, token usage, inference timing, alignment and latent-depth ablations, and a GSM8K case study.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds Llama evaluations, component ablations, representation-diversity measurements, and debugging analyses.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix A.2 revises the alignment computation by multiplying the ridge solution by 1/beta, absent from v1 Appendix A.1. Appendix F also introduces optional parallel text probes for debugging. The core latent-generation and KV-memory-transfer architecture remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, AIME24/25, GPQA-Diamond, MedQA, ARC-E/ARC-C, MBPP+, and HumanEval+. The new backbone evaluations, ablations, and debugging cases reuse this existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 7 adds two evaluated comparison variants: Latent Reasoning + Text Communication and Text Reasoning + Latent Communication. The original Single, Sequential TextMAS, and Hierarchical TextMAS comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: The reported output limits change from 2,048 tokens for general tasks and 8,096 for harder tasks to task-specific limits including 4,096 for MedQA/code, 8,192 for GPQA, and 20,000 for AIME. v3 also adds two Llama configurations, a hybrid comparison retaining only 128 decoded communication tokens, and a manually annotated 100-case debugging study. The PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds analyses separating final-agent token savings, quantifying representation diversity, replacing the two core components individually, and examining debugging correctness and failures (Appendices D–F and I). Alignment visualization adds Qwen3-14B; the existing Qwen3-8B analysis moves to Figure 11. The earlier depth analysis and beehive case study are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces a descriptive correctness-association analysis, reporting conditional proportions with explicit denominators for 80 correct and 20 incorrect final answers in Table 8. Three-independent-run averaging remains unchanged, and no confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: The original Qwen benchmark entries are unchanged after matching the renumbered tables. v3 adds Llama results and numerical findings on final-agent tokens, diversity, hybrid variants, and debugging. For example, Table 4 reports sequential ARC-E accuracy of 91.2% for LatentMAS versus 89.6% for TextMAS on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; this is a newly evaluated configuration, not a performance gain over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces the token-index distribution model with bounded semantic combinations and an output-scale parameter beta. Theorem A.1 removes the distinct-row and nonsingular-alignment assumptions, changes the Wasserstein bound, and supplies a revised proof and alignment derivation. The main expressiveness, information-preservation, and complexity theorems remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claim of training-free collaboration combining latent reasoning with lossless working-memory transfer, together with the same expressiveness, complexity, and headline performance claims. The additional backbone evaluations strengthen support for the existing generality claim.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations concerning the joint contribution of reasoning and communication, shorter final-answer decoding, generalization across model families, and debugging text as a faithful probe capable of locating errors. The existing heterogeneous-agent qualification merely moves from Appendix C.3 to G.

D1.justification: v3 provides a norm-based beta calculation, describes parallel debugging outputs, names the added Llama checkpoints, and identifies Qwen3-14B as the backbone for the retained depth analysis. Existing backend, hardware, evaluation-processing, prompt, and repository-access information is largely retained.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H add focused discussion of latent model collaboration and visual latent reasoning, including new citations such as Latent Visual Reasoning, Monet, and SWE-agent. Embodied-MAS surveys and Transformer Copilot are removed. The central positioning as training-free unification of latent reasoning and communication remains.

P1.justification: The established exposition is largely retained, with local rewrites, shorter section titles, separate efficiency and in-depth-analysis sections, and relocation of related work and discussion. Appendix A reverses the order of justification and derivation, and prompt headers rename Judger to Solver.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main-text layout and substantially rearranges displays, including moving the hierarchical benchmark table into the appendix. It adds Tables 4–8, reorganizes alignment plots, redisplays existing performance summaries, and removes Figure 8's accompanying numerical table while retaining its plot.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central mechanism through component ablations, non-Qwen evaluations, and direct accounting of final-agent token savings—questions not directly tested in v1. Quantitative diversity analysis and the generalized alignment argument further improve assessability. These gains are tempered by revised budget descriptions accompanying unchanged original scores and by debugging correlations that do not establish causal faithfulness, but the overall evidential improvement remains substantial.
